title: One very high value caps the percentage axis at 200%
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in one location (workplace) with the data below.
  3. You use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. A one-off very high Billing Efficiency month for one advisor exists: one invoiced work order today whose Service Advisor has nothing else invoiced this month, with one labor line of 1.00 hour assigned to a technician who clocked exactly 0.25 hours on it (1.00 / 0.25 x 100 = 400%).
  5. The location also has other advisors with ordinary monthly figures under 200% over the last twelve months, so most plotted points are at or below 200%.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. Set the Billing Efficiency pill to Last 12 Months.
  3. Click View details on the Billing Efficiency tile.
  4. Hover each point and count how many read 200% or less and how many read more than 200%.
  5. Read the top label of the left-hand axis.
  6. Hover the point of the advisor seeded above for this month (it sits at the very top edge).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Most points read 200% or less (e.g. 60 of 62 points), and at least one reads above 200%.
  • The axis tops out at 200%: its highest label reads 200%.
  • The very high point is drawn clipped at the top edge of the chart (its line runs off the top), but hovering it shows its true value, e.g. 400%.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9581 (Story 9, Chart Behavior); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 9. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, screenshots of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28) board 05_Billing_After (an axis capped at 200% with one line running off the top), used for on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. When the highest value on the chart is at or below 200% the axis simply fits the data and no cap applies.”
  • S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. When the highest value on the chart is at or below 200% the axis simply fits the data and no cap applies.”
  • S9-R3: “A value drawn above the axis cap is clipped at the top of the chart but still shows its true value on hover.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
